references.text: The preceding verse introduces the cloud pillar and the fire pillar that the Lord used to lead the people of Israel.
The cloud pillar moves and stands between the Egyptian camp and the Israelite camp, bringing darkness to one side and light to the other.
The Lord looked down on the Egyptian camp through the fire pillar and the cloud pillar and brought confusion upon them.
By day the Lord's cloud was over the tabernacle, and by night there was fire in it, visible to all the house of Israel throughout their journeys.
A detailed description of how the cloud covered the tabernacle and appeared as fire at night, and how it guided Israel's journey.
The Lord went before them in a cloud pillar by day and in a fire pillar by night.
Moses reminds the people that the Lord went before them on the way in fire by night and in a cloud by day.
Nehemiah confesses that God led them with a cloud pillar by day and a fire pillar by night.
The cloud pillar did not depart from them by day, and the fire pillar gave light to the path they were to travel by night.
The psalm describes how God guided the people with a cloud by day and with fiery light all through the night.
God spread out a cloud as a covering and fire to give light at night.
The prophecy that the Lord will create a cloud by day and smoke and the shining of a flaming fire by night over Zion.
Paul refers to how all the fathers were under the cloud and passed through the sea, and were baptized into Moses in the cloud.
It highlights the consequence of uninterrupted guidance: the people waited for God's sign before breaking camp.
